2. Plaintiffs-Respondents' claim as described in the scheduled to the plaint are covered by R.S. Khatian No. 132,P, +.2, 370,291, R.S. and P.S. Plot No. 904,906,907,928,908 corresponding to B.S. Khatian No. 256,203,356,32 B.S. Plot No. 847,833,834, 17477, 17476 measuring 48 Shatak or 24 gandas. 

 3. The plaintiff Abdullah Chowdhury and two others instituted other suit No. 09 of 1999 against the defendant No. 1 Bank and 3 others contending that the suit property was originally belonged to one Fazar Bibi and R.S. Khatian stands recorded in her name. She gifted the property to her daughter Ramija Khatun and grandson Mir Ahmed by a deed of gift on 11.06.1936. P.S. Khatian stands recorded in their names. They transferred the property to Haji Kala Mia by Patta No. 459 dated 14.01.1957. Haji Kala Mia died leaving 2 wives, Amina Khatun and Rowshon Akther, 5 sons Kamal Akther, Shah Alam, Abul Kalam, Mahbub Alam and Aziz Mia, 2 daughters Nurjahan Begum and Laila Begum. All these heirs of Haji Kala Mia transferred their inherited property to plaintiff Abdullah Chowdhury. Shamiuzzaman, Kabir Ahmed, Sunil Kanti Deb and others by different deeds being No. 5799 dated 20.05.1977, 7297 dated 20.06.1977, 5094 dated 05.05.1977, 7627 dated 24.06.1977. Sunil Kanti transferred his purchased land to plaintiff Abdullah Chowdhury by Registered deed No. 14086 Dated 15.11.1978. Plaintiff Abdullah Chowdhury,Samiuzzaman and Kabir Ahmed partitioned the property by Registered deed dated 28.11.1978. Abdullah sold three gandas to plaintiff No. 3 Alia Begum by Registered deed dated 11.04.1998. Kabir Ahmed sold 6.91 gandas to plaintiff No. 2 Tahera Begum. B.S. Khatian stands recorded in their names. 

 5. The defendant No. 1 Janata Bank contested the suit by filing written statement contending inter-alia that the property covered by R.S. Plot No. 902,904,906,907 belonged to Neamat Khan and Sadat Khan, and R.S. Khatian was recorded in their name accordingly. Defendant No. 2-4 are the heirs of R.S. recorded owner. The B.S. Khatian No. 427 stands recorded in the name of defendant No. 2-4 which is covered by B.S. Plot No. 516,518, M, 863. The defendants No. 2-4 mortgaged the property to the defendant No. 1 (Bank) as security against loan granted to M/s Chowdhury Enterprise and for realization of Bank dues, the Bank defendant No. 1 instituted mortgage suit No. 35 of 1995 in the 1s' Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong, which was decreed and the said decree was put into execution in Execution Case No. 27 of 1998, in which, an auction notice was published in the daily Azadi on 04.04.1999. The plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No. 06 of 1999 under Order 21 Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was rejected on contest. There after Plaintiff-Respondents filed the instant Other Suit No. 09 of 1999 for declaration indirectly challenging the validity of the decree passed in Mortgage Suit No. 35 of 1995. 

 9. Mr. Mahmudul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant, submits that the suit is barred by Section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003. The Property mortgaged to the Bank are totally different from the land claimed by the plaintiff. The property claimed by the plaintiffs through Fazar Bibi did not belong to her as R.S. Khatian except R.S. Plot No. 928, Patta deed dated 14.01.1957 is not a valid deed to create tenancy right as on the date of execution, no such document could be executed due to bar under section 75 A of the SAT Act. The learned Advocate further submits that the trial court misconceived and misconstrued the evidence on record and arrived at a wrong findings. As such, the impugned judgment and decree are liable to be set aside and on the question of maintainability of a fresh suit filed by 3'd party, learned Advocate for the appellant referred the case of Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Shongtha defendant-appellant -Vs- Rahman Textail Mills Ltd. and others reported in 51 DLR(AD) page 221, Noor Islam defendant-petitioner —Vs- Agrani Bank plaintiff-respondent reported in 49 DLR(AD) page 135 and M/s Shikandars Jute Mill Ltd. petitioner —Vs- Sonali Bank and others respondent reported in 18 BLD(AD) page 268. 

 10. Mr. Nowraz M.R. Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiffs-respondents submits in reply that suit property originally belonged to Fazar Bibi for which R.S. Khatian stands recorded in her name. She gifted the property to her daughter Ramija Khatun and grandson Mir Ahmed by a deed of gift dated 10.06.1936 and accordingly P.S. Khatian was recorded in their names. They transferred the property to Haji Kala Mia by Patta dated 14.01.1957. Heirs of Kala Mia transferred their inherited property to plaintiff Abdullah Chowdhury, Shamiuzzaman, Kabir Ahmed, Sunil Kanti Deb and others by different deeds. Sunil Kanti Deb teransterred his purchased land to plaintiff Abdullah Chowdhury. Abdullah Chowdhury, Samiuzzaman and Kabir Ahmed partitioned the property by registered deed dated 28.11.1978. Abdullah Chowdhury sold 3 gandas to plaintiff No. 3 Alia Begum, Kabir Ahmed sold 6.91 gandas to plaintiff No. 2 Tahera Begum and B.S. Khatian has been recorded in their names. Plaintiffs have not mortgaged the suit property to the Janata Bank. The learned Advocate further submits that the trial court considering facts of the case and evidence, oral and documentary, available on record correctly decreed the suit by the impugned judgment dated 18.08.2005. On the question of maintainability, the learned Advocate has referred the case of Chaina Arzoman Banu appellant —Vs- Rupali Bank Ltd. and others reported in 14 BLD(AD) page 321, Directorate of Enforcement appellant -Vs- Deepak Mahajan and another Respondents reported in A.I.R. 1994(Sc) page 1770 and D. Salbaba-Petitioner Vs-Bar Council of India and another-Respondents Reported in A.I.R. 2003(Sc) page 2502. 

 11. We have gone through the impugned judgment passed by the trial court along with the evidence and exhibits available on record. On hearing the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the appellants and respondents side and considering the pleadings of the parties, it appears that the basis of the plaintiff's, title is R.S. Khatian No. 132 and 132 and 132/1, 370 (Exhibit 1, 1(Kha) and 1 (Ga)). According to plaint case, these Khatians stand in the name of Fazar Bibi. On perusal, we find that R.S. Khatian No. 132, and 132/1(Exhibit 1 and 1(Ka)) stand recorded in the name of the heirs of Neamat Khan and Sadat Khan. R.S. Khatian No. 370 Exhibit I (Ga) with Plot No. 928 measuring an area of 2 decimals was recorded in the name of Fazar Bibi and as such Fazar Bibi has had no right, title and interest in R.S. Plot No. 902,904,906 and 907 to transfer by any deed of gift. 

 12. On perusal of deed of gift dated 10.06.1936 Exhibit 7(Gha), we find that Fazar Bibi gifted to Ramiza Bibi 1.86 acres of R.S. Plot No. 906,907 of R.S. Khatian No. 132 in which she had no title according to A.S. Khatian. Moreover, in R.S. Khatian No. 132 quantum of land is .76 decimal, but she made a gift for 1.86 acres. Deed of gift Exhibit 7(Gha) shows that Fazar Bibi gifted the property covered by Plot No. 906,907 and 928 out of which she had title only in R.S. Plot No. 928 measuring an area of 2 decimal of land, Moreover, the plaintiffs of the suit are claiming R.S. Plot No. 904 which is not in the deed of gift at all. So, she had no transferable interest in that plot. The learned Judge of the trial court erroneously found that the properties mortgaged to the Bank are not the same property claimed by the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs' vendors are not the owner of the property mortgaged to the Bank. The trial court has not discussed the case of the defendant in its true prespective and decreed the suit finding that the property mortgaged with the Bank are the property of the plaintiffs.
